contents.text: The subject and the verb in a sentence or clause must agree in number.

header.text: When a subject is singular, use a singular verb. Singular verbs usually end in -s.

contents.text: Sarah visits her grandmother.
Brian teaches art history.

header.text: When a subject is plural, use a plural verb. Plural verbs usually do not end in -s.

contents.text: Kyle and Jessie walk home.
Those brownies smell delicious.

header.text: Subject-verb agreement is usually determined by the simple subject. Remember that the simple subject and the verb aren't always adjacent.

contents.text: The excitement of the fans is palpable.
The violinists who performed the duet work together quite often.

header.text: Some sentences are inverted, meaning the subject follows the verb.

contents.text: Original: Your blueberry pancakes are here.
Inverted: Here are your blueberry pancakes.
